lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, eight a.m. Her dad has called a family meeting.
**Dad:** **Operation Beach Day**! East Coast Park. Every minute planned. I have even drawn a **graph**.
**Kavya:** Dad, it's a beach. You just go to the beach.
**Mum:** He's been up since five. Let him have this.
**Ah Boy:** Is there a graph for **ice cream**?
**Dad:** Ice cream is at **three p.m.** Not before. It's on the graph.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about the beach. It's about the line on Dad's graph.
**Lionel:** Lionel. A **straight line**. I go on **forever**, in both directions. And I **never bend**.
**Lionel:** My **gradient** shows my mood. Happy: **uphill**, positive. Sad: **downhill**, negative. Bored: **flat**. Zero.
**Ah Boy:** Can you go **straight up**?
**Lionel:** Vertical? Then **nobody** can calculate my gradient. Never. Ask me. That.
**Lionel:** One family. One beach. One perfectly straight plan. I'll keep it straight.
**Narrator:** Rise Over Run. Episode 12: Operation Beach Day.
**Narrator:** Nine a.m. East Coast Park. The park map is a **grid**. The bike kiosk is the **origin**.
**Dad:** Team! Our picnic spot is at **(2, 5)**. Go!
**Ah Boy:** Found it! **5** across, **2** up!
**Ex:** Ex. I go **across**. And I go **first**.
**Why:** Why. I go **up** or **down**. Why am I always **second**?
**Ex:** **(2, 5)** is **2 across**, then **5 up**. **(5, 2)** is somewhere else: the **toilets**.
**Kavya:** **Along the corridor, then up the stairs.** x first, then y.
**Kavya:** Negative x: **left**. Negative y: **down**. The beach is at **(−3, −2)**.
**Why:** Four **quadrants**, numbered **anticlockwise** from the top right. The beach is in the **third**.
**Priya:** Priya. Best friend. New **drone**. Beach **A** to jetty **B(5, 4)**, and it stops **halfway**.
**Kavya:** A to B is **8 across** and **6 up**. Halfway is **4 across** and **3 up**: **(1, 1)**.
**Ah Boy:** I got **(2, 2)**! I just **added** them!
**Why:** Why didn't you **halve** them? Divide by **2**!
**Dad:** I'm at **(−3, 4)**. The ice-cream cart is **halfway** to Mum, at **(2, −1)**. Where's Mum?
**Kavya:** Dad to the cart: **5 right**, **5 down**. Same step again: Mum is at **(7, −6)**.
**Mum:** Correct. And no, Ah Boy, it is **not** three p.m. yet.

chapters.title: Mum's rope
chapters.short: x = a, y = b, y = x

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Ten a.m. Mum ropes off the picnic area. Precisely.
**Mum:** From **x = −1** to **x = 5**, and from **y = −3** to **y = 2**.
**Dad:** **x = −1**? That's on the x-axis. Rope goes **across**.
**Ex:** No! In **x = −1**, I'm **stuck** at −1, and y can be **anything**. **Vertical!**
**Why:** I'm free! Up! Down! Wheee!
**Kavya:** The line runs parallel to the **other** axis. **x = a** is **vertical**; **y = b** is **horizontal**.
**Ex:** So the **y-axis** is the line **x = 0**, and the **x-axis** is **y = 0**.
**Mum:** Width: 5 − (−1) = **6**. Height: 2 − (−3) = **5**. Area: **30** square units.
**Mr Tan:** Kavya! Mr Tan, out jogging. The line **y = x** goes right through your mat!
**Mr Tan:** On **y = x** the coordinates are **equal**: (−2, −2), (0, 0), (4, 4). It rises at **45°**.
**Kavya:** And **y = −x** has **opposite** coordinates, like **(2, −2)**. It falls at 45°.
**Mr Tan:** Reflect **(5, 2)** in **y = x** and the coordinates **swap**: **(2, 5)**.
**Ah Boy:** So I wasn't wrong. I was just **reflected**.
**Mr Tan:** Careful with **y = x**. Whatever x says, y just **copies** it.
**Ah Boy:** Whatever x says, y just copies it.
**Narrator:** Eleven a.m. Priya's drone will fly along the line **y = 3x + 2**.
**Priya:** **Table of values**, x from −2 to 2. y: **−4, −1, 2, 6, 8**. Launch!
**Lionel:** It **bent**! Into a **coconut tree**! A straight line **never bends**!
**Kavya:** Check the **differences**: +3, +3, **+4**, **+2**. In a straight-line table they're all the **same**.
**Kavya:** Each step of 1 in x adds **3**. At x = 1: 3 × 1 + 2 = **5**. Not 6.
**Ex:** And at x = −2, **brackets** protect the negative: 3 × (−2) + 2 = **−4**.
**Lionel:** **Table. Substitute. Plot.** Then join with **one ruled straight line**, across the whole range.
**Ah Boy:** Done! I joined the dots in the sand!
**Lionel:** That's not me. That's a **zigzag**. I am **one** line. Drawn with a **ruler**.
**Mr Tan:** Mr Tan, lap two. Is **(−3, −7)** on the line? 3 × (−3) + 2 = **−7**. Yes!
**Mr Tan:** And **(4, 15)**? 3 × 4 + 2 = **14**, not 15. Just **above** the line.
**Priya:** Fixed: **−4, −1, 2, 5, 8**. Relaunch!
**Dad:** It landed on my **sandwich**.
**Narrator:** Twelve noon. The skate park. Ah Boy wants the **steepest** ramp.
**Ah Boy:** Ramp A! It's the **biggest**, so it's the **steepest**!
**Mo:** Mo. Mountain goat. I am the **gradient**. **m** for **mountain**.
**Mo:** Gradient = **rise ÷ run**. How far **up**, divided by how far **across**.
**Priya:** Easy. **Across** over **up**. Ramp A: 4 ÷ 2 = **2**.
**Mo:** **Rise over run!** You **rise** from your seat **before** you **run**. Rise goes on **top**.
**Kavya:** **B** is the steepest. **A** and **C** are **equally** steep, even though A is bigger.
**Dad:** I'll be on ramp C. For the view.
**Mo:** Uphill, left to right: **positive**. Downhill: **negative**. Flat: **zero**. Gradient **3**? Up **3** for every **1** across.
**Cece:** Cece. **Crossing** guard. **c** for **crossing**. Every line crosses the y-axis at my post: **(0, c)**.
**Lionel:** So my full name is **y = mx + c**. In America it's **y = mx + b**. I prefer c.
**Dad:** **y = 5 − 2x**. Gradient **5**. It comes **first**.
**Mo:** The gradient is the number **multiplying x**, **sign included**. m = **−2**, c = **5**. Downhill.
**Ah Boy:** What about a ramp that goes **straight up**?
**Lionel:** The run is **zero**. You **can't divide by zero**. No gradient. I **told** you never to ask.
**Narrator:** One p.m. Lunch on the mat. Kavya's phone is dying.
**Kavya:** It was **80%** at nine. It loses **5%** every **hour**.
**Cece:** Start at **80**: that's my **c**. Lose **5** an hour: **m = −5**. So **B = 80 − 5t**.
**Dad:** I'm joining a **gym**! **$30** to join, then **$25** a month. **C = 25n + 30**.
**Mum:** And **c** is the part you pay even if you **never go**.
**Mr Tan:** Mr Tan, lap three. Lunch quiz! Match **three equations** to **three graphs**. Read the **sign** of m, its **size**, and **c**.
**Kavya:** **Steep uphill**, crossing at 1: y = 3x + 1. **Shallow downhill**, crossing at 4: y = −½x + 4. **45°**, crossing at −3: y = x − 3.
**Lionel:** And now, my **family reunion**! Me, **y = 2x**. My brothers, **y = 2x + 3** and **y = 2x − 2**.
**Lionel:** Same gradient. **Parallel**. We **never meet**. Family reunions are very awkward.
**Priya:** So **parallel** lines have **equal gradients**. Only **c** is different.
**Mr Tan:** Stretch! **No graph**. Find the line through **(1, 5)** and **(4, 14)**.
**Kavya:** m = (14 − 5) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3 = **3**. Subtract in the **same order**, top and bottom.
**Priya:** **y = 3x + 2**. That's my **drone's** line!
**Narrator:** Two p.m. Dad comes back from a run.
**Dad:** I ran **five**! Five **miles**. My watch is from London.
**Mum:** And how many **kilometres** is that?
**Ori:** Ori. The **origin**, **(0, 0)**. I run the **Direct Proportion Club**. Lines get in **through me**.
**Ori:** Miles to km: **y = 1.6x**. **Straight**, through the **origin**: **direct proportion**.
**Kavya:** Up from **5 miles** to the line, then across: **8 km**. **10 miles**: **16 km**. **25**: **40**.
**Ori:** km ÷ miles is always **1.6**. That's **k**, the **gradient**: kilometres per mile.
**Priya:** Phone plans. **Plan P**: **$3** per GB. **Plan Q**: **$6** a month, plus **$2** per GB.
**Kavya:** P: **0 GB**, **$0**. **2 GB**, **$6**. **4 GB**, **$12**. Double the data, double the cost.
**Ori:** Plan Q starts at **$6**. It **misses the origin**. **Not on the list.**
**Ah Boy:** But it's a **straight line**!
**Ori:** Straight is **not enough**. It needs the **origin** too. No input, no output.
**Priya:** Plan P, then. **y = 3x**. I'm on the list.
**Ah Boy:** It's **three p.m.**! **ICE CREAM!**
**Dad:** Then bike hire! Shop X: **$8**, plus **$3** an hour. Shop Y: **$5** an hour, no fixed fee.
**Kavya:** X is **C = 3h + 8**. Y is **C = 5h**, through the origin.
**Kavya:** Where the graphs **cross**, they cost the **same**: 3h + 8 = 5h, so **h = 4**. Both **$20**.
**Dad:** Operation Beach Day says we ride for **six** hours.
**Mum:** Six hours: X is 3 × 6 + 8 = **$26**. Y is 5 × 6 = **$30**. Shop **X**. And we ride for **one**.
**Narrator:** Priya rides to the jetty and back. Her watch draws a **distance–time graph**.
**Lionel:** That's me, in three pieces. Up: **6 km** in **30 minutes**. Flat for **20**. Down: home in **20**.
**Dad:** The flat bit is where she cycles at a **steady speed**.
**Lionel:** Flat means the distance **isn't changing**. She **stopped**. So did I. I had a **nap**.
**Mo:** On a distance–time graph, **gradient = speed**. **Steeper** is **faster**. Going **down** means coming **back**.
**Kavya:** Minutes to **hours** first! Out: 6 km in **½ hour** = **12 km/h**. Back: 6 km in **⅓ hour** = **18 km/h**.
**Ah Boy:** Mine's **curved**! I went faster and faster down the slope!
**Lionel:** That's my cousin, **Curvy**. A curve means the **speed is changing**. We don't talk.
**Kavya:** And where **two** distance–time graphs **cross**, two people **meet**: same place, same time.

chapters.title: The beach saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the beach saves you some marks.
**Ex:** One. **Across first**, then up or down. **(x, y)**. Never (y, x).
**Ah Boy:** Two. **Brackets** for negatives: y = 4 − 3 × (−2) = **10**. Not −2.
**Lionel:** Three. **One ruled straight line** across the whole range. **Never** dot-to-dot.
**Mo:** Four. Downhill means a **minus** gradient. Keep the sign. Goats fall for it.
**Priya:** Five. **Minutes** aren't **hours**. Convert before you find a speed in km/h.
**Dad:** Six. A **midpoint**: add the coordinates, then **halve** both: ÷ 2. Ask Ah Boy.
**Narrator:** Rise Over Run will return.
**Narrator:** Eight p.m. Home. Dad reviews Operation Beach Day.
**Dad:** Everything went **exactly** to plan.
**Ah Boy:** I made a graph too! **Ice creams** against **time**. **Six** ice creams. All at **three p.m.**
**Mum:** What? **SIX?!**
**Lionel:** Vertical... gradient... cannot... be... calculated...
